listenings.text: Okay, so I got it. The internship. I still cannot believe it. Listen, I applied to eleven places. Eleven. And nine of them never answered, which is normal, apparently. The interview was twenty minutes and only three questions were in English: what I study, why I want to work there, and what I do on weekends. That is it. Nothing complicated. So here is my advice, and I am serious about this: prepare four sentences about yourself and say them out loud before the call. Not in your head. Out loud. Because in your head everything sounds perfect.

Good morning. A quick note about the careers fair. It is on Thursday, from ten in the morning until five in the afternoon, in Building B. Twenty-two companies are coming this year, and eight of them are looking for students in their third or fourth semester, so that is most of you. Bring your student card. If you have a CV in English, bring it too, and bring several copies. And one last thing: talk to the small companies. Everybody stands in the queue for the big names and nobody talks to the small ones. Thank you.
